6.question: Which business rules and definitions should the AI know when answering questions about **Opal AI Platform Usage**? We've pre-drafted definitions inferred from your selected concepts, datasets, and metrics — confirm the ones that are accurate, edit any that need adjusting, and add any missing rules.

selected.label: Account Tiers: Paid vs. EAP vs. Non-Paid
selected.description: Three account tiers govern which accounts appear in Opal metrics: (1) **Paid Accounts** — accounts with a signed, active Opal commercial contract; (2) **EAP Accounts** — Early Access Program accounts with Opal access but no commercial contract, used for testing and early feedback; (3) **Non-Paid Accounts** — all remaining accounts with some Opal access but outside the paid or EAP cohorts. Metrics labelled 'Paid Accounts' exclude both EAP and Non-Paid unless otherwise stated.
selected.ai_reasoning: The selected metrics explicitly split across Paid, EAP, and Non-Paid tiers (e.g., 'Opal - Median Credits - Paid Accounts' vs. 'EAP Accounts' vs. 'Non Paid Accounts'), so the AI must understand this classification to correctly scope any question about 'Opal accounts'.

selected.label: Active User / Account Definitions — DAU, WAU, MAU, L90D
selected.description: A user is counted as **Daily Active (DAU)** if they triggered at least one Opal event on the calendar day in question. **Weekly Active (WAU)** = at least one event in a rolling 7-day window. **Monthly Active (MAU)** = at least one event in a rolling 30-day window. An account is counted as active in the **L90D** window if any user within that account triggered at least one Opal usage event in the past 90 calendar days. All windows are rolling, not calendar-period aligned, and are anchored to SST Max Date.
selected.ai_reasoning: The selected stickiness metrics (DAU/WAU and WAU/MAU) and both account utilization KPIs (EXP L90D, CMP L90D) depend on these exact thresholds; without them the AI cannot correctly interpret or reproduce engagement figures.

selected.label: Thread = Atomic Unit of Opal Engagement
selected.description: A **thread** is a single end-to-end Opal conversation session — the primary unit of platform engagement. One thread may contain zero agent invocations (pure conversational chat) or multiple agent invocations. Thread count is the top-level volume KPI and the denominator for all agent-adoption rate metrics (e.g., '% of Threads with an Agent Triggered'). A user opening Opal and sending a message always starts a new thread; a thread is not re-used across sessions.
selected.ai_reasoning: Thread is the foundational unit referenced across all selected usage datasets and metrics; the AI must understand this definition to correctly interpret questions about volume, depth, and agent adoption without confusing threads with sessions, events, or generations.

selected.label: OOTB Agents vs. Custom Agents
selected.description: **OOTB (Out-of-the-Box) agents** are Optimizely-shipped agents bundled with the standard Opal product, catalogued in 'Product - Opal OOTB Agents' with release dates and product mappings. **Custom agents** are built by customers or partners for specific use cases, catalogued separately in 'Product - Custom Agents'. Metrics scoped to 'OOTB Agent Triggered' exclude custom agents and vice versa. The AGENTS_PER_THREAD_BUCKET dimension counts invocations of both types combined unless an explicit agent-type filter is applied.
selected.ai_reasoning: The selected Opal Agent Registry concept exists specifically to make this distinction; the graph has two separate catalog datasets (OOTB Agents vs. Custom Agents), and two separate adoption metrics split on this boundary, so the AI must understand it to avoid conflating agent categories.

selected.label: Opal Cannibalization vs. Opal Incremental ARR — Do Not Sum
selected.description: **OPAL_CANNIBALIZATION** = ARR that shifted from an existing Optimizely product line subscription into an Opal contract. It represents revenue retained at the company level but attributed to Opal at the expense of the originating product's ARR — it is a zero-sum transfer, not growth. **OPAL_INCREMENTAL** = net-new ARR directly attributable to Opal that would not have existed under any prior product line — this is genuine new revenue. These two columns must **never be summed together** into a single 'Opal ARR impact' figure; they answer fundamentally different questions and require separate analysis.
selected.ai_reasoning: The Product ARR Bridge & Opal Cannibalization concept is a core selected concept, and misinterpreting these two columns — e.g., summing them to show 'total Opal revenue contribution' — would produce a materially misleading figure that conflates growth with revenue migration.

selected.label: ARR Movement Figures Are Constant-Currency (CCFX) — Not Nominal
selected.description: All ARR movement columns in the product bridge dataset (PRODUCT_ARR_CHANGE_CCFX, OPAL_CANNIBALIZATION, OPAL_INCREMENTAL) are expressed in **constant-currency FX (CCFX)** — exchange-rate fluctuations are removed so that period-over-period changes reflect genuine business activity, not currency movements. When comparing Opal's ARR contribution across periods, always use CCFX figures. Point-in-time ARR snapshots from the ARR Report or DHW_SST_ARR_REPORT may be in local/nominal currency; do not mix CCFX and nominal values in the same analysis.
selected.ai_reasoning: The ARR Churn dataset description explicitly references constant-currency records, and the PRODUCT_ARR_CHANGE_CCFX column naming confirms CCFX adjustment; without this rule the AI may mix nominal and constant-currency figures in YoY or QoQ comparisons.

selected.label: Generation = Discrete AI Content-Creation Request (≠ Thread, ≠ Feature Event)
selected.description: A **generation** is a discrete AI content-creation request processed by an Opal agent — for example, drafting marketing copy, proposing experiment variants, or generating audience recommendations. It is distinct from a **thread** (the conversation container) and from a **fine-grained feature event** (a UI interaction such as opening the sidebar or clicking a button). A single thread may produce zero, one, or many generations. Generation volume and agent-level generation breakdowns should be sourced from 'Product - Opal Generation Data' or 'OPAL_DAILY_AGENT_ACCOUNT_GENERATION_USAGE', not from the thread-level usage tables.
selected.ai_reasoning: The Opal AI Content Generation concept has its own dedicated event sources distinct from platform usage tables; without this definition the AI may incorrectly use thread-level data to answer generation-volume questions or vice versa.

selected.label: Opal Entry Points: Purple Button, Chat Sidebar, Standalone Agents
selected.description: Opal is accessible via multiple product entry points: the **Purple Button** (in-context AI assist embedded in the CMP and EXP UI), the **Opal Chat sidebar** (general-purpose conversational interface), and **Standalone Agents** (direct agent access outside a standard product workflow). Platform-level usage metrics in DWH_OPAL_DAILY_PRODUCT_ACCOUNT_USAGE and DWH_OPAL_DAILY_USER_ACCOUNT_USAGE aggregate across ALL entry points unless the question explicitly filters to one. The fine-grained usage dataset (DWH_OPAL_FINE_GRAINED_USAGE) is the only source that captures entry-point granularity.
selected.ai_reasoning: Several selected metrics explicitly reference the Purple Button separately from specialized agents (e.g., 'Total Accounts Using Purple Button - L90D - Paid Accounts'), making entry-point taxonomy essential for the AI to distinguish partial from total Opal engagement.

selected.label: Account Utilization % Formula: Active Paid Accounts ÷ Total Eligible Paid Accounts (L90D)
selected.description: The **Account Utilization %** KPI (for both CMP Opal and EXP Opal) is computed as: (number of paid accounts with at least one Opal usage event in the last 90 days) ÷ (total paid accounts eligible for Opal in that product). 'Eligible' means the account holds a valid Opal entitlement in the product, regardless of whether they have ever used it. The denominator comes from 'Total Accounts Eligible - Paid Accounts' metrics; the numerator from 'Accounts Utilization % - L90D - Paid Accounts'. L90D is a rolling window anchored to SST Max Date, not calendar month-end.
selected.ai_reasoning: The denominator definition ('eligible' vs. 'all accounts') is the most common source of incorrect utilization rate calculations; making this explicit ensures the AI computes and describes EXP and CMP adoption rates consistently with how they are defined in the selected metrics.

selected.label: SST Max Date Is a Data-Freshness Sentinel, Not a Business Metric
selected.description: **SST Max Date** represents the latest snapshot date for which Opal usage data has been loaded into the source tables. It is a data-freshness indicator used to anchor 'as-of' queries and prevent counting zero-activity days not yet ingested. It should never be interpreted as a business event date or included in trend calculations. If SST Max Date lags the current calendar date by more than 2 days, data should be flagged as potentially stale and downstream metrics treated with caution.
selected.ai_reasoning: SST Max Date is the sole freshness metric selected in step 4, and questions about 'current' Opal usage must be anchored to it — the AI must not confuse it with a KPI or treat missing data between SST Max Date and today as zero-activity.

selected.label: Opal Is Cross-Product: CMP, EXP, and Future Products
selected.description: Opal is not a standalone product — it is an AI layer deployed across multiple Optimizely product lines. For this topic, the primary host products are **CMP** (Content Marketing Platform) and **EXP** (Experimentation). Agent invocations are mapped to their parent product via 'Product - Opal Product Mapping'. Cross-product Opal usage (where a single account uses Opal within both CMP and EXP) should be counted once at the account level but separately at the product-account level to avoid double-counting in utilization metrics.
selected.ai_reasoning: The Opal Agent Registry maps agents to parent products (CMP, EXP), and the selected datasets are partitioned at the product-account grain; without this rule the AI may double-count accounts that use Opal across multiple products when answering 'how many accounts use Opal?' questions.
